intro:
Use it to hold one thing on a page: a plan, a setting, a summary, an item in a grid. It is a bordered surface with a header, a body and a footer, and the header keeps a place in its top trailing corner for a control that belongs to the whole card.

The padding lives on the parts, not on the card. A picture that should reach the card's edges goes straight inside it with `overflow-hidden` on the card.

It has no state and no event handlers of its own, so it renders as a server component.

For a list of rows under a title, use [Frame](/docs/web/components/frame).
usage:
<Card>
  <Card.Header>
    <Card.Title>Create a workspace</Card.Title>
    <Card.Description>Start on the free plan and invite your team later.</Card.Description>
    <Card.Action>
      <Button variant="link">Sign in</Button>
    </Card.Action>
  </Card.Header>
  <Card.Content>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Work email</FieldLabel>
      <Input type="email" />
    </Field>
  </Card.Content>
  <Card.Footer variant="panel">
    <Button>Create workspace</Button>
  </Card.Footer>
</Card>

parts.Header: The title, the line under it, and the action. It switches to two columns when there is an action.
parts.Title: What the card is about. An `h3` by default; `as` picks another level to fit the page.
parts.Action: A control for the whole card, held in the header's top trailing corner whatever order it is written in.
parts.Content: The body. It starts with top padding of its own when the card has no header.
parts.Footer: The row at the bottom. `variant="panel"` makes it a darker band set into the card, for actions.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `size="sm"` tightens the padding and the title, for a card in a dense grid.

examples.title: Footers
examples.description: A `plain` footer continues the card. A `panel` footer is a band set into its bottom, which reads as what you do with the card rather than more of what it says.

examples.title: Image
examples.description: A picture placed first in the card reaches its edges. Give the card `overflow-hidden` so the picture takes its top corners; the parts after it keep their own padding.

examples.title: In a list
examples.description: `as="li"` puts the card in a list, and `Card.Title`'s `as` sets the heading level to fit the page around it.

notes:
`as` on the card renders it as a `div`, `article`, `section` or `li`. Use `article` for a card that makes sense on its own and `li` inside a list.

`Card.Title` is a heading so the page outline includes it. Set its level with `as`, from `h2` to `h4`, or `div` for a card that should stay out of the outline.
